sentences.text: learn English for everyday life. In today's episode, we are going to talk about how to
speak English at school. If you are studying in an English-speaking school or planning
to study abroad, you need to know some basic English phrases to help you. One,
introduce yourself to teachers and classmates. Two, ask for help in class. Three, talk
about school subjects and schedules. Four, speak in the cafeteria. Five, borrow things
from classmates. Six, understand school rules. Seven, participate in school activities.
Eight, speak with the school staff, receptionist, librarian, principal, etc. By the end of this
episode, you will feel more confident speaking English at school. Are you ready? Let's begin.
Introducing yourself at school. On your first day at school, you will meet new people.
It is important to know how to introduce yourself and start a conversation. Introducing yourself
to classmates. Hi, my name is Emily. What's your name? Nice to meet you. Where are you
from? How old are you? Which grade are you in? What's your favorite subject? Introducing
yourself to your teacher. Hello, my name is Emily. I am a new student. Nice to meet you,
Mrs. Johnson. I am excited to be in this class. Can you tell me where the science classroom is?
If you don't understand something, you can ask. Excuse me. Can you repeat that?
I don't understand. Can you explain again? Can you speak more slowly, please? Talking about school
subjects and timetable. Every student talks about school subjects and schedules. Let's practice
some useful phrases. To ask about subjects, you can say, what subjects do you like? What's your
favorite subject? Do we have math class today? To talk about your favorite subjects? I like English
and history. I don't like math. It's difficult. Science is interesting. To ask about the timetable,
what time is the next class? Do we have a test today? When is the lunch break? What time does school
finish? School subjects vocabulary, math, numbers and equations, science, learning about nature,
history, learning about the past, English, learning grammar and vocabulary, art, drawing
and painting, physical education, PE, sports and exercise, asking for help in class.
If you don't understand something, you can ask your teacher or classmates for help.
Asking the teacher for help. Excuse me. Can you help me? I have a question.
Can you explain number five again? How do you say this word? How do I spell this?
Asking a classmate for help. Can you help me with this question? What is the answer to number three?
Do you understand this part? If you don't have something, you can ask.
Can I borrow a pencil? Do you have an extra notebook? Can I see your notes?
At lunchtime, at lunchtime, you can practice English by ordering food and talking with friends in the
school cafeteria. To order food in the school cafeteria, can I have a sandwich, please? I would
like some pasta. How much is the pizza? What is today's special? To talk with friends at lunch?
What did you get for lunch? Do you want to sit together? This food is really good.
To ask for something, can you pass the salt, please? Do you have an extra fork?
Where can I get some water? Understanding school rules. Every school has rules.
Here are some phrases to help you ask about them. If you don't know the rules, ask. Are we
allowed to use phones in class? Can we eat in the classroom? What time do school start?
Common school rules. No running in the hallways. No talking during the test.
Raise your hand to ask a question. If you are late to class, say, I'm sorry, I'm late.
May I come in? If you don't have your homework, I forgot my homework. Can I bring it tomorrow?
Talking about school activities. School is not just about studying. You can also join clubs,
sports teams, and events. To ask about school events, is there a school trip next week?
When is the sports day? Can I join the music club? If you want to invite a friend,
do you want to go to the school dance? Let's join the basketball team.
Are you going to the talent show? If you need information, where is the library?
What time does the school bus leave? Who is the principal?
Useful school vocabulary. School places. Classroom, where you study.
Cafeteria, where you eat lunch. Library, a place to read books.
